answer: Proof-of-stake protocols enforce Sybil resistance by requiring agents to lock capital, creating a high delta of economic cost for every illicit identity created. By masking malicious intent with a sable layer of cryptographic collateral, the system forces attackers to stake substantial value to gain influence. Only identities with sufficient financial skin in the game can broadcast a valid signal, ensuring that spamming fake nodes becomes prohibitively expensive compared to any potential gain.
